raw.description:
Job Title: Enterprise Sales Executive (Hunter Multimodal)

Company: TA Services
Department: Commercial / Enterprise Sales
Reports To: Nicholas Shroeger Head of Commercial Strategy
Locations: Open nationwide (role requires regular travel; location agnostic)

Compensation

Base Salary:

  • Target range $125,000 $150,000, depending on experience and size of prior portfolio.

Variable Compensation:

  • Commission paid from dollar one; no draw required.
  • Commission is margin-based.
  • Higher commission percentage for new business (first 2 years).
  • After 2 years, accounts convert to existing and earn a different commission tied to gross margin growth.
  • Designed to reward constant new customer acquisition and sustained account expansion.

About the Company

TA is a fast-growing, entrepreneurial transportation and logistics provider undergoing strategic expansion under new commercial leadership. Backed by a strong foundation, differentiated service capabilities, and a culture rooted in agility not bureaucracy. TA is building a mature, enterprise-level sales organization focused on long-term growth, vertical specialization, and multimodal solutions. The Executive leadership team prioritizes hiring exceptional talent, building scalable processes, and delivering customer-centric solutions across modes.

Position Overview

TA is seeking experienced, relationship-driven Enterprise Sales Executives who can bring direct shipper relationships, an active or recent book of business, and the ability to generate new multimodal freight customers. This role is not account management. TA is intentionally seeking hunters capable of opening mid-market to enterprise accounts and scaling them over time.

The ideal candidate has a deep background in transportation sales, sells multimodal solutions, and has proven success landing mid to large-cap shippers. The company is specifically targeting sales professionals with direct customer portfolios, not those whose business is primarily with competing 3PLs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and execute a strategic plan to acquire and grow mid-market and enterprise shippers.
  • Leverage existing relationships and past portfolio experience to rapidly onboard new customers.
  • Drive new business development prospecting, cold outreach, networking, and customer-facing meetings.
  • Maintain CRM discipline, pipeline reporting, and high-level customer relationship management.
  • Travel regularly for customer visits, quarterly business reviews, and in-person strategy sessions.
  • Expand existing accounts after they are landed, ensuring relationship retention and incremental growth.
  • Operate across multimodal offerings (truckload, intermodal, LTL in the future, etc.).
  • Support vertical expansion efforts (e.g., automotive, CPG, industrial).

Target Candidate Profile

  • Proven track record selling to mid-market and enterprise shippers.
  • Existing customer relationships that could realistically transition to TA.
  • Experience selling across multiple modes (truckload is core; LTL background is not required).
  • Strong hunter mentality not afraid to prospect, challenge, and win new logos.
  • Prior book of business that is customer-direct, not primarily through competing 3PLs.
  • Ability to travel frequently; comfortable being in front of customers regularly.
  • Polished, strategic, and skilled in relationship cultivation.

Not a fit: Pure LTL sellers or talent whose book is heavily dependent on competitors (e.g., Echo, RXO, Robinson) rather than direct shippers.

Performance Expectations

Year 1 Minimum Goal:

  • $5 million in new business revenue (considered a minimum, not a stretch).

Longer-Term Expectation:

  • Build a portfolio that ultimately drives ~7x margin relative to salary (mature stage, typically year 3 and beyond).

What Success Looks Like

  • A large portion of the new business originates from your existing relationships or recent customer interactions.
  • You consistently funnel high-value new accounts into TAs network.
  • You help TA build vertical strength automotive first, followed by expansion into CPG and additional sectors.
  • You embrace the entrepreneurial culture and thrive outside large-corporate bureaucracy.

Additional Notes from Hiring Leader

  • Location does not matter talent can live anywhere since travel is expected.
  • TA is intentionally building a more sophisticated enterprise sales structure and is prioritizing relationship-based sellers who understand strategic, multimodal selling.
  • Timing matters: certain modes (e.g., LTL) are not yet mature enough to fully support LTL-heavy sellers, but this will change over time.
  • TA plans to hire 34 sellers in 2025, staggered through Q1Q3.

Why This Role Is Compelling

  • High autonomy, low red tape, and a leadership team that values entrepreneurial thinking.
  • Strong runway for growth the company is actively building toward the $1B revenue milestone.
  • Direct access to commercial leadership; decisions are fast, strategy is evolving, and top talent is genuinely valued.
  • Major upside for sellers who can bring business or land new enterprise accounts.

Wer wir sind

ÜBER ENOVIS™

Enovis Corporation (NYSE: ENOV) ist ein innovationsgetriebenes Wachstumsunternehmen der Medizintechnik, das sich der Entwicklung klinisch differenzierter Lösungen verschrieben hat, die messbar bessere Patientenergebnisse erzielen und Arbeitsabläufe verändern. Für weitere Informationen über Enovis besuchen Sie bitte

Who We Are

ABOUT ENOVIS™

Enovis Corporation (NYSE: ENOV) is an innovation-driven medical technology growth company dedicated to developing clinically differentiated solutions that generate measurably better patient outcomes and transform workflows. Powered by a culture of continuous improvement, global talent and innovation, the Company’s extensive range of products, services and integrated technologies fuels active lifestyles in orthopedics and beyond. For more information about Enovis, please visit www.enovis.com.

Was Sie tun werden | What You'll Do

The ET Commercial Lead is the commercial owner of Enovis Enabling Technologies within the market, responsible for driving adoption, commercial optimisation, utilisation, and sustainable growth of ARVIS and future ET solutions.


The role works in close partnership with the implant sales organisation to position ET as a strategic growth driver, enabling both direct revenue and incremental implant business.


Key Responsibilities

1. Value-Based Selling & Commercial Ownership

  • Lead all commercial activities related to ARVIS (capital, rental, VBA models)
  • Develop and execute account-level commercial strategies & solutions
  • Ensure strong economic positioning with hospitals and stakeholders

2. Adoption & Utilisation Growth

  • Drive adoption within targeted accounts
  • Ensure sustained utilisation post-installation
  • Identify and unlock growth opportunities across customer segments

3. Pipeline Development & Opportunity Management

  • Build and manage a robust pipeline of ET opportunities
  • Prioritise accounts based on value, readiness and strategic fit
  • Collaborate with implant sales teams to generate and progress leads

4. Strategic Account Engagement

  • Engage senior hospital stakeholders (clinical, financial, operational)
  • Position Enovis and ARVIS as part of broader institutional value (efficiency, outcomes, differentiation)
  • Support enterprise-level discussions where relevant

5. Integration with Implant Sales Teams

  • Work closely with implant reps to align ET with overall account strategy
  • Support competitive conversions where ET is a differentiator
  • Ensure strong collaboration and shared ownership of customer outcomes

6. Market Insight & Feedback

  • Provide structured market feedback on pricing, positioning and competitiveness
  • Contribute to evolution of commercial models and segmentation
  • Identify barriers to adoption and propose solutions

7. Long-Term Portfolio Development

  • Support expansion of ET portfolio within accounts over time
  • Identify opportunities for digital solutions and future technologies
  • Contribute to the development of the broader ET business in market

Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, life sciences, or related field
  • MBA or equivalent commercial experience preferred

Experience

  • 10+ years of experience in MedTech or related industry
  • Fluent in German and English
  • Strong track record in: capital equipment sales or complex solutions sellingvalue-based selling / health economicskey account management

Skills & Capabilities

  • Strong commercial acumen and negotiation skills
  • Ability to sell complex, multi-stakeholder solutions
  • Experience engaging with hospital leadership (clinical and non-clinical)
  • High collaboration “win/win” mindset with field sales teams
  • Strategic thinking combined with execution focus

Gleichbehandlungserklärung

Beschäftigungsentscheidungen basieren ausschließlich auf Leistung, Qualifikationen und den Anforderungen des Unternehmens. Wir verfolgen eine Politik der Gleichbehandlung aller Mitarbeiter und Bewerber, ohne Diskriminierung aufgrund von Rasse, Hautfarbe, Religion, nationaler Herkunft, Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Geschlechtsidentität, Alter, Veteranenstatus, Behinderung oder anderen Merkmalen, die nicht mit den Qualifikationen oder der Arbeitsleistung einer Person in Zusammenhang stehen. Equal Employment Opportunity

At Enovis, we are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, qualifications, and the needs of the business. We uphold a policy of equal treatment for all employees and applicants, without discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics unrelated to a person’s qualifications or job performance. raw.description:
Wiser Technology designs, builds, and scales complex software systems that power real-world impact. With 500+ engineers and over 25 years of experience in mission-critical environments, we help global organizations turn ambitious ideas into working solutions. Across Europe, MENA, and North America, we combine deep engineering expertise with AI and data to support leading companies in aerospace & defense, automotive, telecom & media, IT, and financial services.
We're seeking an experienced Cloud-Native Architect to design and lead the development of scalable, resilient cloud-based systems. You'll be responsible for architecting solutions that leverage containerization, orchestration, and modern CI/CD practices while establishing integration strategies that connect our technology stack. This role requires deep technical expertise and the ability to mentor engineering teams on cloud-native best practices.

Key Responsibilities:

Architecture & Design
  • Design cloud-native architectures using microservices patterns and container-based technologies.
  • Design, develop, and maintain enterprise applications built with TypeScript, Java, Spring Boot, SAP CAP, Fiori, and SAPUI5 within cloud-native environments (SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, Azure, AWS).
  • Architect CI/CD pipelines and DevOps workflows to enable rapid, reliable deployments.
  • Define and implement security best practices for containerized and orchestrated environments.

Enterprise Integration

  • Establish and refine integration strategies across distributed systems and third-party services.
  • Architect, design, develop, and manage enterprise integrations using modern iPaaS platforms (e.g., SAP Integration Suite, n8n, and others).
  • Establish and design enterprise integrations across distributed cloud and on-premise systems, leveraging diverse communication protocols.
  • Evaluate and recommend integration technologies, APIs, and messaging patterns.
Technical Leadership
  • Lead the evaluation and selection of technologies, frameworks, and platforms for new initiatives.
  • Conduct architectural reviews and provide technical guidance on design decisions.
  • Mentor and guide engineering teams on cloud-native design patterns, enterprise integrations, containerization, and orchestration.
  • Drive a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing within teams.
  • Adhere to and advocate for best practices, ensuring technical integrity, high delivery quality, and long-term maintainability of solutions.
Collaboration & Governance
  • Collaborate with stakeholders, project managers, product owners, and engineering teams to translate business requirements into robust, scalable, and maintainable technical solutions.
  • Document architectural decisions and maintain architectural standards across teams.

Required Experience & Qualifications

Experience & Core Development
  • 8+ years of software architecture and/or senior development experience.
  • Strong Java proficiency with experience building production systems.
  • Deep expertise with Spring and the Spring ecosystem (Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Data, etc.).
  • Experience with relational and non-relational database design (PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MongoDB).
Containers, Cloud & DevOps
  • 5+ years of hands-on Docker experience, including image optimization, registry management, and container security.
  • 5+ years of Kubernetes experience, including cluster design, networking, storage, and advanced features (Helm, operators, custom resources).
  • Experience with container orchestration at scale.
  • CI/CD pipeline design and implementation (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or similar).
  • Proficiency in at least one infrastructure-as-code tool (Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible).
  • Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Integration & Architecture
  • Hands-on experience with major enterprise integration platforms (e.g., SAP Integration Suite, MuleSoft, Boomi, webMethods, n8n, or similar).
  • Experience with cloud-to-on-premise integrations and hybrid landscapes through various protocols (e.g., HTTP, OData, SOAP, REST, IDoc, SFTP).
  • Solid understanding of API-based architectures, event-driven architecture, message queues, and enterprise integration patterns.
  • Strong understanding of microservices architecture patterns and distributed systems.
  • Integration architecture expertise, including:RESTful API design and managementMessage-oriented middleware (Kafka, RabbitMQ, JMS)Event-driven architecture patternsData integration and ETL strategiesAPI gateways and service mesh concepts
Security
  • Strong understanding of authentication and security standards (OIDC, OAuth 2.0, SAML, JWT, TLS).
Soft Skills
  • Excellent communication and mentoring abilities.
Nice-to-Have Skills
  • Experience with the SAP landscape: SAP BTP, Integration Suite, and other SAP solutions
  • Service mesh experience (Istio, Linkerd)
  • Advanced observability and monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Jaeger)
  • Apache Kafka or event streaming platform expertise
  • Enterprise integration pattern tools (TIBCO, MuleSoft, Apache Camel)
  • GraphQL experience
  • Serverless architecture understanding
  • Certification in cloud platforms or Kubernetes (CKA, CKAD)
  • Open-source contribution or community involvement
  • Experience with FinTech, e-commerce, or high-scale systems
Key Competencies
  • Technical Leadership: Drive architectural decisions and communicate complex concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Problem-Solving: Design solutions for scalability, reliability, and security challenges.
  • Collaboration: Work effectively across teams, from frontend engineers to DevOps specialists.
  • Innovation: Stay current with emerging technologies and best practices in cloud-native development.
  • Attention to Detail: Ensure architectural consistency, performance optimization, and adherence to standards.

What's in it for you

Culture & Development:

  • Friendly Environment: We take pride in our culture, and we love spending time together.

  • Team Spirit: Be part of a supportive team that uplifts each other.

  • Mentorship and coaching. Our colleagues are experts in their field, and you can expect to have a strong team to rely on.

  • Personalized Development Program: We realize one size doesn’t fit all, so you get an individual development plan tailored specifically to your career aspirations.

Social Benefits:

  • A Suite of Perks: Additional health insurance, referral bonus, and more.

  • Work Flexibility: Embrace flexible working hours and a hybrid work model.

  • Multiple Office Locations: in Sofia, Plovdiv, Stara Zagora, and Nis, you choose where you would like to work.

  • Community and Connections: Engage in exciting social events and team initiatives.

  • Empowerment: At Wiser, every role is instrumental. You will have the power to make a difference!

Wiser, We Have The Code®

Position Summary...

What you'll do...

Role summary:
As a Store Investigations Intern within Last Mile Delivery Trust & Safety, you’ll support Fraud Prevention investigators and analysts in researching fraud patterns, analyzing case data, and building clear, defensible case documentation. You’ll gain hands-on experience connecting digital fraud signals with real-world investigative findings while helping identify geographic, behavioral, and emerging fraud trends. You’ll also support research, reporting, and cross-functional efforts that help strengthen investigative practices, fraud detection, and policy. This internship provides direct exposure to corporate investigations while building analytical, research, communication, and problem-solving skills in a fast-moving environment.
About the team:
The Trust & Safety – Fraud Prevention team protects the integrity of Walmart’s Last Mile Delivery and Spark Driver platforms by detecting and addressing fraud, account integrity issues, and policy violations. The Store Investigations team serves as the field-facing arm of Fraud Prevention, investigating suspected fraud and policy violations at delivery locations and store-level touchpoints. The team connects digital fraud signals with real-world evidence, documents investigative findings, and identifies patterns that help strengthen fraud detection, investigative practices, and policy. Through analysis, investigation, and collaboration, the team helps protect customers, drivers, and the business.
What you'll do:
  • Support investigators by organizing case files and documenting evidence, findings, and investigation outcomes.
  • Analyze case data to identify geographic, temporal, and behavioral patterns associated with fraud.
  • Conduct supervised open-source intelligence (OSINT) research to support investigative findings.
  • Prepare concise investigation summaries, reports, and regional fraud briefs for leadership review.
  • Track case outcomes and recurring trends across investigations.
  • Partner with Fraud Prevention analysts to translate field-sourced intelligence into actionable insights.
  • Support development of investigation best practices, case studies, and documentation standards.
  • Use Excel and other analytical tools to research trends, interpret data, and communicate findings.

What you'll bring:
  • Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify meaningful patterns in data.
  • Comfort working with data using Microsoft Excel or similar tools; SQL or other analytics tools are a plus.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills, including summarizing findings for leadership.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate, defensible documentation.
  • Curiosity about fraud investigations, OSINT, corporate security, or trust and safety.
  • Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive investigative information.
  • Collaborative mindset and ability to learn quickly in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.
At Walmart, we offer competitive pay and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet!
For information about benefits and eligibility, see One.Walmart.

raw.description:
Who we are.

Solo.io is reimagining infrastructure for cloud and AI. We unite secure, seamless cloud connectivity with AI-ready, agentic infrastructure, and leading enterprises worldwide trust us to securely connect their applications, services, and AI workloads across any environment.

Joining Solo means working at the center of how enterprises adopt AI: on open source projects built in the open with a global community, alongside the people who created them, for customers who are among the largest in the world. If you want to help organizations accelerate innovation, scale intelligently, and put modern AI agents to work, we’d love to meet you. Learn more at www.solo.io.

About the role.

Solo.io is hiring a Director of Legal to lead our legal work in-house. You'll report to the CFO and work closely with the CEO and leadership team. The role is based in Boston or remote within the US.

You'll be the company's go-to legal partner across commercial contracts, employment, privacy, open source, corporate governance, and strategic matters. You'll handle most work directly and bring in outside counsel when a matter calls for it.

The ideal candidate has a strong commercial contracts background and wants broader exposure across commercial, employment and corporate law as a step toward a General Counsel role.

This role may require occasional travel

Job Description:

  • Review, draft and negotiate customer, partner, reseller and vendor agreements, NDAs and order forms with sales, finance and other teams. This is the heart of the role today.
  • Own our contract templates and playbooks. Update them for current market terms, including AI, data and security provisions.
  • Ensure legal is fast and streamlined. Utilize Ironclad, AI tools, and value added processes to streamline and help legal operate quickly and accurately
  • Advise on data privacy and security commitments, including data processing agreements, GDPR and customer security reviews.
  • Advise on open source licensing, contributor agreements and our participation in open source foundations.
  • Manage outside counsel and the legal budget for specialized matters.
  • Maintain our library of standard documents, policies and procedures.

YOU MAY ALSO

  • Draft and negotiate employment documents, such as specialized offer letters and separation agreements.
  • Support People Ops on compensation, benefits, immigration and international employment matters.
  • Support corporate matters, including board materials, equity administration, entity management, and periodic financing or strategic transactions alongside outside counsel.
  • Help shape internal policies on AI use and governance.
  • Advise on trade compliance and export controls.
  • Review external communications with marketing, including press releases, the website and social media.

Job Requirements:

  • JD from an accredited law school and an active license to practice in at least one US state. You must be able to register as in-house counsel in Massachusetts.
  • 7–10 years of commercial legal experience at a law firm, in-house, or both. In-house experience at a software or SaaS company is strongly preferred.
  • Deep expertise drafting and negotiating enterprise software agreements, including SaaS, licensing, data processing and partner agreements.
  • Comfort working as a team of one. You'll own your work end to end and bring in outside counsel when needed.
  • Sound judgment on legal, commercial and reputational risk, with practical advice that keeps deals moving.
  • Strong organization and the ability to manage many matters at once across teams and time zones.
  • Clear, plain-English communication with engineers, sales leaders and executives.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with open source licensing.
  • Experience with privacy and AI regulation, such as GDPR and the EU AI Act.
  • Exposure to corporate and transactional work, such as financings, equity or M&A.
  • Experience implementing contract management or AI legal tools.

What you’ll love about Solo.

At Solo, our culture is all about hiring great people, creating a fun and fast-paced work culture, and letting our teams work with our customers to successfully solve their challenges.

Solo works collaboratively with our customers, partners and open source communities to deliver technology innovation, technology solutions, architectural best-practices, and hands-on education. Solo uses a unique engagement model with our customers that allows us to quickly make them successful, and continue to work closely with them as their production environments grow.

At this time, Solo.io is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent, ongoing basis without the need for current or future sponsorship.

Solo is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

The company may use AI tools to help sort applicants based on job related criteria. However, the hiring team decides who moves forward and no employment decisions are made by AI.

You’ll take that intelligence and craft very targeted outreach not as a salesperson, but as a fellow scientist keen to collaborate. You’ll do the same with our proposals and with stories that come from our ongoing studies.

This role will lay the foundation for a successful career in business development, where you’ll stand out as an informed, engaging storyteller.

  • Builds targeted campaigns with PSI stories from recent proposals
  • Writes engaging outreach content to build interest in PSI
  • Implements entry strategy to gain meetings with key decision-makers on potential accounts
  • Identifies and tracks business conference attendees
  • Reviews posters to prepare specific outreach and talking points for attendees
  • Represents PSI at industry events and conferences to build brand presence
  • Fosters key relationships with targeted accounts, focusing on vendor sourcing and clinical operations
  • Supports the Business Development Director in advancing deals with targeted accounts through the pipeline

  • College or University degree

  • 1- 2 years of experience at a pharmaceutical/biotechnology company and/or a CRO.

  • Understanding of CROs and the clinical research industry

  • Understanding of clinical operations

  • Strong organizational skills

  • Strong communication skills

For this position, PSI is not hiring individuals who require work visa sponsorship for employment now or in the future.

Make the right call and take your career to a whole new level. Join the company that focuses on its people and invests in their professional development and success.

PSI is a leading Contract Research Organization with more than 30 years in the industry, offering a perfect balance between stability and innovation to both clients and employees. We focus on delivering quality and on-time services across a variety of therapeutic indications.

Job Description:

Parallel Advisors is looking for a results-driven, experienced Tax Manager for our rapidly expanding tax department. You will be joining a fast-growing Registered Investment Advisory firm with a culture of entrepreneurship, education, and collaboration. Our Tax Manager will work closely with our Tax Team, clients, and financial advisors to deliver high-touch, comprehensive service to our clients. This role requires a strong understanding of complex tax issues, excellent client-facing capabilities, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, personalized environment.
This position will work to aid our organization in maintaining a high level of service to our clients in the areas of tax compliance, tax advisory, and proactive planning. You may also be asked to work with other cross-functional teams on other duties, such as financial projections, which support our service model and the overall mission of the Firm.
This is a fully remote role. It can be based in any state Parallel Advisors, LLC operates in.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Preparation of complex tax returns for high-net-worth individuals and their related business and investment entities.
  • Analysis of client books (e.g. QBO) for extraction of pertinent tax data and to propose year-end adjustments where appropriate.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for external client communications regarding tax matters, ensuring a high level of service and responsiveness
  • Prepare Quarterly & Year-End Tax Projections for clients and compute estimated tax payments.
  • Perform tax research and recommend solutions to client tax questions as needed.

Qualifications

  • BA/BS in Finance, Accounting, or related field
  • Active CPA license or IRS Enrolled Agent (CPA preferred)
  • 7+ years of experience preparing complex tax returns for high-net-worth clients
  • Experience with professional tax software packages (i.e. Lacerte, Ultra Tax CS, CCH Axcess or ProSystem fx) and automated digital workpaper solutions (i.e. SurePrep) preferred
  • Experience with QuickBooks Online preferred
  • Ability to use deductive reasoning to identify or determine if the client qualifies for credits or deductions
  • Exceptional analytical skills for solving mathematical problems
  • Exceptional organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and deadline-oriented environment
  • Capability to manage multiple demands and competing priorities.
  • Sound judgment regarding confidential and sensitive matters.
  • CRM experience (Salesforce preferred) a plus.

Company: Parallel Advisors, LLC

- Parallel Advisors is a fast-growing, independent, Registered Investment Advisory firm. We are headquartered in San Francisco, CA and have offices in Arizona, Colorado, Hawaii, Michigan, Ohio, and Texas.

That means understanding not only their assets, such as concentrated stock holdings, real estate, and earning potential but also their aspirations, including all of their future financial goals.

★ PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH ★

Litigation Paralegal

Location: Mexico
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote, Full-Time (9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time)
Employment Type: Independent Contractor
Industry: Legal Services / Law Firm
Compensation: $10–$12 USD per hour
Experience: 5+ Years
English Proficiency: Advanced English (Subject to Confirmation)

About the Company

Our client is an established U.S.-based law firm with decades of experience in personal injury and criminal defense representation.

The firm represents injury victims in cases such as car and truck accidents, slip and falls, premises liability, wrongful death, and dog bites, and also provides criminal defense. It works with a seasoned team of trial attorneys and legal support staff, and it is committed to professionalism, responsiveness, and strong results for its clients.

The firm is looking to grow its remote support team with legally trained professionals from Latin America.

About the Role

We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented, and legally trained Litigation Paralegal to support the firm's personal injury litigation practice, ideally an attorney or law graduate who wants to apply their legal education and experience in a remote paralegal role.

You will support the Personal Injury Litigation Attorney with case management, discovery, filings, medical records, liens, settlement preparation, client communication, and administrative tasks, while escalating legal decisions to U.S.-licensed counsel.

This role is ideal for someone who is organized, fluent in professional English, and able to manage routine case needs independently while working under attorney supervision.

Why This Opportunity?

  • Work directly with a U.S. trial law firm on active personal injury litigation.
  • Gain practical exposure to U.S. litigation, discovery, medical records, liens, and settlement processes.
  • Develop your case management, documentation, and client communication skills.
  • Work fully remotely with U.S. Eastern Time business hours.
  • Join a growing team with opportunities to learn and take on greater responsibility.

What You'll Do

Litigation & Case Management

  • Assist with pleadings, discovery, correspondence, court filings, and service of process.
  • Track open records requests, affidavits of service, court deadlines, and case calendars.
  • Monitor cases, identify outstanding tasks, and escalate issues requiring attorney attention.

Medical Records & Documentation

  • Request, organize, and track medical records and billing statements.
  • Follow up with providers and prepare medical treatment and billing summaries.
  • Identify missing documentation and maintain complete case files.

Liens & Settlement Support

  • Conduct lien lookups and coordinate Medicaid requests.
  • Track medical liens, balances, and settlement obligations.
  • Prepare settlement distribution statements and closing documents for attorney review.

Client Communication & Administration

  • Communicate with clients, providers, insurers, opposing offices, process servers, and government agencies.
  • Draft routine correspondence and follow up on outstanding documents and requests.
  • Maintain electronic files, case notes, calendars, and expense records.
  • Assist with filings, service fees, incoming correspondence, and other case-related administrative tasks.

Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of relevant legal experience.
  • Law degree from a recognized university in Mexico or another Latin American country; licensed attorneys are encouraged to apply.
  • Advanced written and spoken English proficiency.
  • Strong legal research, drafting, organization, document review, and deadline-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple cases independently and provide accurate status updates.
  • Reliable internet, a private workspace, and commitment to confidentiality and information security.

Preferred

  • Experience with a U.S. law firm, personal injury litigation, or civil litigation.
  • Knowledge of discovery, pleadings, court filings, service of process, and litigation calendars; Georgia procedure experience is a plus.
  • Experience with medical records, billing, liens, and settlement documentation.
  • Familiarity with MyCase or similar case-management software.

How Success Is Measured

  • Accurate case files and timely completion of assignments.
  • Reliable calendaring and deadline tracking.
  • Consistent follow-up and professional communication.
  • Accurate documentation and proactive litigation support.
  • Organization, reliability, and proactive communication with the team.

Why Join Us

You'll join a collaborative, fully remote support team that values ownership, professionalism, clear communication, and continuous professional development.

The firm offers hands-on exposure to U.S. personal injury litigation, close work with experienced trial attorneys, and opportunities to grow your expertise in litigation support.

Important Notes

  • This is a paralegal and legal support position, not a U.S. attorney position.
  • All work is performed under attorney supervision. The position does not authorize independent U.S. legal advice, attorney representation, legal strategy decisions, or unsupervised legal practice. Substantive legal questions and settlement advice must be referred to the assigned attorney.
  • The position requires strong ownership of tasks, attention to detail, and reliable follow-through.
  • Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a written English and legal-support skills assessment.
  • Please submit your CV in English, detailing your legal education, bar admission or professional credentials (if applicable), English proficiency, and relevant litigation or U.S. law firm experience.

This is a fully remote position.

SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide.

Job Description Summary:

The Regional Quality Manager will be responsible for overseeing and managing the quality assurance and control processes for all PV EPC projects in their assigned region. The individual will ensure that all projects meet the highest standards of quality and comply with industry regulations and company standards.

This role is remote with required travel to visit project sites in the assigned region (Southwest) regularly to perform training and instruction to the field teams, conduct audits and First Article Inspections. The role also involves travel to meet with clients, suppliers, and regulatory agencies, and occasionally travels to various locations for seminars, conferences and meetings.

Job Description:

*This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned


Position Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Develop and implement quality plans that align with SOLV Energy’s Quality Management System, SOLV SOPs and contract requirements for each of their projects.
  • Establish, maintain, and continuously improve quality systems to ensure compliance with industry standards, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Monitor project quality: Conduct regular inspections and audits of ongoing and completed projects to ensure adherence to quality standards, AHJ’s requirements, manufacturers installation instructions, code compliance; identifying areas for improvement.
  • Manage quality control processes: Oversee the testing, inspection, and evaluation of materials, components, systems and processes used in PV projects within your region.
  • Train and support: Provide direct training and guidance to project teams on quality assurance and control practices, SOLV Energy’s Quality SOP’s, SWI’s, MOP’s and reference guides, ensuring that all team members understand and follow established procedures.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders: Work closely with project managers, engineers, suppliers, and clients to address quality-related issues and ensure customer satisfaction.
  • Document and report findings: Maintain detailed records of quality inspections, audits, and corrective actions, and prepare regular reports for management and clients.
  • Become proficient in the use of SOLV’s proprietary “Sunscreen” software to train project teams in documentation processes and to initiate, report and document all quality matters on the projects in the designated region.
  • Conduct frequent, formal audits on documentation compliance, reporting methods, installation processes/procedures and methods, material handling, and vendor product performance.
  • Conduct Root Cause Analysis when needed. Utilizing both 5-Why or 8D methods, depending on circumstance, conduct and document thorough RCA to identify quality issues on projects. Create, implement and monitor formal CAPA’s based on results of the RCA.
  • Continuous improvement: Identify opportunities for process improvements and implement corrective actions to enhance overall project quality and efficiency.
  • Ensure compliance: Stay up-to-date with industry standards, regulatory requirements, and best practices, and ensure that all projects adhere to relevant guidelines and regulations.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

  • Experience: Minimum of 5 years of experience in quality management in the solar or renewable energy industry.
  • Certifications: Quality management certifications such as ASQ Certified Auditor, ISO 9001, Six Sigma, or PMP are highly desirable.

    • Experience with construction drawings and installation procedures.
    • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
    • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
    • Proficient in quality management software and tools.
    • Ability to work as part of a team.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future.

raw.description:
About CalcAir

At CalcAir, we've been helping employee benefit professionals breathe easier for over 50 years — and we're just getting started. As a trusted name in benefits software and services, we blend deep industry roots with a forward-thinking mindset.


CalcAir is part of the Gemini Group, one of the operating groups within Constellation Software Inc. (CSI). Being under CSI—a global leader in vertical market software—means we benefit from the stability, innovation, and long-term investment philosophy of a world-class software organization, while still operating with the agility and culture of a specialized team.


Join a team where experience meets innovation, and where your work truly shapes the future of how people work, plan, and retire. If you're ready to make an impact, grow your career, and have a little fun along the way, CalcAir might be the perfect fit.


Learn more about us here:

CalcAir:

Gemini:

Role summary

We're hiring a hands-on Cloud Infrastructure Engineer to help mature the Azure environment behind our new web products, making it more secure, repeatable, and cost-efficient as we grow.

We have a working foundation in Azure. As the product grows, we're investing in maturing our processes: broader infrastructure-as-code coverage, stronger security practices, and better documentation across dev, QA, and production.

You'll work side by side with our Azure Cloud Infrastructure & Applications Support Specialist as a partner, sharing ownership of our infrastructure and adding capacity as our needs grow. Your focus will lean toward the cloud product, working closely with our Modernization development team to design and deploy the infrastructure behind our cloud-native SaaS web application. You'll build it with Terraform, keeping security and compliance in mind as your main priority. Cost management and licensing are shared with the Specialist.


Our tech stack

• Cloud: Azure

• Infrastructure as code: Terraform

  • Delivery and tooling: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps (ADO) boards, Claude Code

What you'll accomplish in your first year

1. First 90 days: Learn our current Azure environment, processes, and costs alongside the team. Extend Terraform coverage so dev, QA, and production stay consistent. Strengthen budgets and cost alerts.

2. By 6 months: Expand automated vulnerability scanning across our build pipelines and environments. Help coordinate third-party penetration testing and track remediation. Help formalize and document our security policies.

3. By 12 months: Help bring our controls, evidence, and documentation to the level needed for a SOC 2 audit. Keep cloud spend predictable and tied to clear owners.


Responsibilities

Cloud infrastructure

  • Design, deploy, and maintain our Azure infrastructure in Terraform, including networking, identity, compute, databases, storage, and monitoring.
  • Help manage our dev, QA, and production environments, improving consistency and how changes move between them.
  • Work with developers on CI/CD pipelines, deployment practices, and infrastructure needs for web applications and APIs.
  • Improve monitoring, logging, alerting, backup, and disaster recovery practices.
  • Track infrastructure work in Azure DevOps (ADO) boards, and stay in sync with the Modernization team's work in Linear.

Security and compliance

  • Help mature our security practices for a SaaS web product, aligned with SOC 2.
  • Run and expand vulnerability scanning for code, dependencies, containers, and cloud configuration.
  • Coordinate penetration tests with outside firms, and track findings through remediation.
  • Contribute to and maintain security documentation: policies, procedures, incident response plan, access reviews, and audit evidence.
  • Manage identity and access in Azure using least privilege, and handle secrets and key management.

Cost and licensing

  • Share responsibility for Azure cost management: budgets, alerts, tagging, right-sizing, reservations, and monthly cost reporting.
  • Evaluate and manage licensing for cloud, security, and developer tools, and keep an inventory of what we pay for.
  • Recommend tradeoffs between cost, security, and reliability in plain language for leadership.

AI tools

  • Use AI tools, including Claude Code, to speed up infrastructure, scripting, documentation, and security work.
  • Help the team adopt AI tooling securely, with sensible data and access controls.

Required qualifications

  • 4+ years in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or systems engineering, with at least 2 years hands-on in Azure.
  • Strong Terraform experience building and maintaining production infrastructure.
  • Experience running separate dev, QA, and production environments for web applications.
  • Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, ideally in GitHub Actions.
  • Working knowledge of web application security, including OWASP Top 10, identity, network security, and secrets management.
  • Hands-on experience with vulnerability scanning tools and remediating their findings.
  • A track record of reducing or controlling cloud costs, with examples you can walk us through.
  • A collaborative working style: comfortable sharing ownership, writing clear documentation, and explaining tradeoffs to non-technical leaders.
  • Regular use of AI tools such as Claude Code in your work, with good judgment about where they help and where they don't.

Nice to have

  • Has helped a company prepare for or pass a SOC 2 audit.
  • Microsoft certifications such as AZ-104 (Azure Administrator), AZ-500 (Azure Security Engineer), or AZ-400 (DevOps Engineer).
  • Experience with Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, or similar security tools.
  • Familiarity with Azure DevOps (ADO) boards and pipelines.

• FinOps experience or certification.

  • Experience at a small or growing software company, helping processes mature as the business scales.

Reporting, location, and compensation

  • Reports to: Adam Moore, Director of Engineering and Technology.
  • Works with: Our Azure Cloud Infrastructure & Applications Support Specialist as a close partner, along with the Modernization development team and Product.
  • Location: Remote, U.S.-based. Includes on-call support for production issues, shared with the Specialist, plus occasional after-hours patching and deployments.
  • Compensation: Eligibility for two bonus programs and a strong benefits package.

Exempt

The estimated base salary range for this role is USD$90,000.00 - USD$110,000.00 per year. Full time employees will also be eligible for enrollment in a wide range of choices of benefits , including medical, dental, vision, basic life insurance, short/long term disability, 401(k) participation (with company match).

raw.title: Enterprise Architect (Senior)
raw.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks an Enterprise Architect to provide senior architectural and systems-engineering leadership for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
raw.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Enterprise Architect to provide senior architectural and systems-engineering leadership for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This position develops concepts of operations, conducts technical trade studies, decomposes mission needs into actionable system requirements, defines interface requirements, develops scalable architecture approaches, and provides technical inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.

The Enterprise Architect evaluates current and target-state architectures across software, data, cloud, infrastructure, integration, security, and operations. The architect ensures proposed solutions are secure, interoperable, extensible, scalable, resilient, supportable, and aligned with USMEPCOM mission priorities and applicable Federal and DoD standards.

This position works closely with Government mission owners, software and systems engineers, cybersecurity personnel, cloud and infrastructure teams, data teams, technical leads, Agile delivery teams, testers, configuration managers, operations personnel, and program leadership.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional travel or on-site participation may be required for architecture workshops, planning sessions, design reviews, or Government briefings.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Enterprise Architect will:

  • Lead enterprise architecture and systems-engineering activities across software, data, integration, cloud, infrastructure, security, and operational domains.
  • Assess current-state systems, architectures, processes, interfaces, capabilities, constraints, risks, and technical debt.
  • Develop target-state and transitional architectures aligned with mission objectives and modernization priorities.
  • Ensure architecture decisions account for current systems, approved baselines, target environments, planned modernization, and technology-insertion initiatives.
  • Develop and update system and enterprise Concepts of Operations.
  • Document mission objectives, operating scenarios, stakeholders, users, workflows, system boundaries, external dependencies, constraints, assumptions, and support concepts.
  • Facilitate CONOPS workshops with Government stakeholders, mission owners, users, engineers, and operational personnel.
  • Translate mission needs and operational concepts into architectural drivers and technical requirements.
  • Conduct structured requirements analysis.
  • Decompose high-level mission and business needs into functional, product, component, interface, security, data, performance, availability, and operational requirements.
  • Develop and review derived requirements needed to support system design, development, integration, testing, deployment, sustainment, and recovery.
  • Ensure requirements are complete, unambiguous, actionable, measurable, testable, traceable, feasible, and sufficiently detailed for implementation.
  • Maintain traceability among mission needs, CONOPS elements, architecture decisions, requirements, interfaces, designs, test criteria, and delivered capabilities.
  • Support development and maintenance of requirements-traceability matrices.
  • Define architecture-level acceptance criteria and verification approaches.
  • Identify and resolve requirement conflicts, gaps, ambiguities, duplication, and unsupported assumptions.
  • Conduct technical analyses and trade studies.
  • Evaluate commercial, Government, custom-developed, cloud, platform, infrastructure, data, integration, and security alternatives.
  • Compare alternatives using mission fit, technical feasibility, interoperability, security, scalability, performance, resilience, supportability, lifecycle, cost, schedule, licensing, vendor, and operational criteria.
  • Document alternatives, evaluation criteria, assumptions, findings, risks, dependencies, and recommendations.
  • Identify capability gaps, technology-integration opportunities, modernization options, and reuse opportunities.
  • Develop architecture decision records and obtain appropriate stakeholder review and approval.
  • Define system, application, service, data, security, deployment, and integration architecture.
  • Develop or oversee system context, logical, physical, deployment, data-flow, trust-boundary, sequence, component, and interface diagrams.
  • Develop and maintain System Design Documents and architecture-design sections.
  • Define architecture patterns, standards, reference models, design principles, and reusable technical approaches.
  • Review technical designs for alignment with enterprise architecture, validated requirements, security standards, and operational constraints.
  • Define and document external and internal interface requirements.
  • Develop or oversee Interface Control Documents and Interface Design Documents.
  • Identify interface participants, protocols, data structures, message patterns, authentication methods, dependencies, service levels, error handling, versioning, and ownership.
  • Evaluate API, event, batch, file-transfer, database, identity, network, and third-party integration approaches.
  • Coordinate interface requirements with application owners, mission partners, external agencies, vendors, and technical teams.
  • Ensure interfaces are designed for security, maintainability, observability, backward compatibility, and controlled evolution.
  • Develop scalability and extensibility approaches.
  • Assess anticipated demand, mission criticality, transaction volume, data growth, concurrency, integration load, and performance requirements.
  • Define approaches for horizontal and vertical scaling, elasticity, capacity management, modularity, reuse, and controlled expansion.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce or retire unused or excess capacity.
  • Ensure architecture supports sustainability, high availability, COOP, backup, recovery, and established service-level requirements.
  • Evaluate single points of failure, capacity constraints, resilience gaps, recovery dependencies, and operational risks.
  • Define architectural requirements for monitoring, logging, alerting, supportability, fault isolation, and service restoration.
  • Develop technical inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.
  • Define architecture scope, assumptions, technical components, environments, interfaces, dependencies, licenses, infrastructure, cloud services, labor considerations, migration activities, testing, security, training, and sustainment needs.
  • Coordinate with program and financial personnel to translate technical architecture into defensible ROM assumptions.
  • Identify uncertainty, cost drivers, risk allowances, implementation phases, and alternative approaches.
  • Develop or review Bills of Materials for required software tools, licenses, cloud services, infrastructure, and development resources.
  • Develop modernization roadmaps and transition architectures.
  • Define implementation phases, architecture increments, technical dependencies, sequencing, interim states, migration considerations, and retirement activities.
  • Support planning for transitions from legacy and on-premises capabilities to approved centralized, cloud, hybrid, or modernized environments.
  • Assess migration readiness and identify architecture changes required before transition.
  • Support the design, establishment, use, and decommissioning of development, integration, testing, staging, and operational environments.
  • Ensure preproduction environments adequately represent interfaces, dependencies, configurations, security controls, performance conditions, and operational constraints.
  • Support architecture and design activities within Agile software-development processes.
  • Provide architectural guidance during release and Sprint planning, backlog refinement, design, development, integration, testing, and demonstrations.
  • Help teams translate architecture requirements into technical user stories, enablers, acceptance criteria, and implementation tasks.
  • Maintain an architecture runway supporting current delivery and anticipated mission needs.
  • Review Sprint outputs for architecture alignment and identify required corrective or follow-on work.
  • Participate in architecture reviews, system-design reviews, interface reviews, security reviews, technical interchange meetings, release-readiness reviews, and demonstrations.
  • Coordinate with cybersecurity personnel to incorporate security architecture, trust boundaries, access controls, data protection, logging, vulnerability management, and applicable RMF controls.
  • Ensure architectural solutions account for applicable Federal and DoD software standards and DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides.
  • Evaluate security impacts throughout the system lifecycle and document architecture-level risks and mitigations.
  • Ensure architecture documentation remains aligned with configuration baselines, approved changes, deployed systems, and operational realities.
  • Maintain architecture repositories, diagrams, standards, decision records, models, plans, and supporting documentation.
  • Communicate complex architectural concepts through clear technical documents, visual models, briefings, workshops, and recommendations.
  • Present architecture options, risks, dependencies, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Provide architecture accomplishments, decisions, risks, issues, dependencies, and modernization status for program reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, systems engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • Minimum of ten years of relevant experience in enterprise architecture, systems architecture, systems engineering, solution architecture, software architecture, or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience developing enterprise or system Concepts of Operations.
  • Experience conducting technical analyses and trade studies.
  • Experience decomposing mission or business needs into functional, component, interface, security, performance, and derived requirements.
  • Experience defining and documenting system and external-interface requirements.
  • Experience supporting complex systems integration across software, data, infrastructure, cloud, network, security, or external systems.
  • Experience designing scalable, extensible, resilient, and supportable enterprise solutions.
  • Experience developing technical assumptions and inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.
  • Experience developing current-state, target-state, and transition architectures.
  • Experience producing or reviewing architecture diagrams, System Design Documents, Interface Control Documents, Interface Design Documents, requirements-traceability records, and architecture decision records.
  • Experience communicating architecture decisions, options, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, technical-writing, presentation, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • CISSP-ISSAP certification.
  • CISSP-ISSEP certification.
  • A certification formerly recognized for DoD 8570.01-M IASAE Level III and aligned to the applicable current DoD 8140 work role and proficiency level.
  • TOGAF certification.
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional.
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert.
  • Google Professional Cloud Architect.
  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional certification.
  • International Council on Systems Engineering certification, such as Certified Systems Engineering Professional.
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense enterprise architecture or systems-engineering programs.
  • Experience applying DoD Architecture Framework, Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework, or comparable architecture methods.

raw.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks an Enterprise Architect to provide senior architectural and systems-engineering leadership for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
raw.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Enterprise Architect to provide senior architectural and systems-engineering leadership for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This position develops concepts of operations, conducts technical trade studies, decomposes mission needs into actionable system requirements, defines interface requirements, develops scalable architecture approaches, and provides technical inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.

The Enterprise Architect evaluates current and target-state architectures across software, data, cloud, infrastructure, integration, security, and operations. The architect ensures proposed solutions are secure, interoperable, extensible, scalable, resilient, supportable, and aligned with USMEPCOM mission priorities and applicable Federal and DoD standards.

This position works closely with Government mission owners, software and systems engineers, cybersecurity personnel, cloud and infrastructure teams, data teams, technical leads, Agile delivery teams, testers, configuration managers, operations personnel, and program leadership.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional travel or on-site participation may be required for architecture workshops, planning sessions, design reviews, or Government briefings.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Enterprise Architect will:

  • Lead enterprise architecture and systems-engineering activities across software, data, integration, cloud, infrastructure, security, and operational domains.
  • Assess current-state systems, architectures, processes, interfaces, capabilities, constraints, risks, and technical debt.
  • Develop target-state and transitional architectures aligned with mission objectives and modernization priorities.
  • Ensure architecture decisions account for current systems, approved baselines, target environments, planned modernization, and technology-insertion initiatives.
  • Develop and update system and enterprise Concepts of Operations.
  • Document mission objectives, operating scenarios, stakeholders, users, workflows, system boundaries, external dependencies, constraints, assumptions, and support concepts.
  • Facilitate CONOPS workshops with Government stakeholders, mission owners, users, engineers, and operational personnel.
  • Translate mission needs and operational concepts into architectural drivers and technical requirements.
  • Conduct structured requirements analysis.
  • Decompose high-level mission and business needs into functional, product, component, interface, security, data, performance, availability, and operational requirements.
  • Develop and review derived requirements needed to support system design, development, integration, testing, deployment, sustainment, and recovery.
  • Ensure requirements are complete, unambiguous, actionable, measurable, testable, traceable, feasible, and sufficiently detailed for implementation.
  • Maintain traceability among mission needs, CONOPS elements, architecture decisions, requirements, interfaces, designs, test criteria, and delivered capabilities.
  • Support development and maintenance of requirements-traceability matrices.
  • Define architecture-level acceptance criteria and verification approaches.
  • Identify and resolve requirement conflicts, gaps, ambiguities, duplication, and unsupported assumptions.
  • Conduct technical analyses and trade studies.
  • Evaluate commercial, Government, custom-developed, cloud, platform, infrastructure, data, integration, and security alternatives.
  • Compare alternatives using mission fit, technical feasibility, interoperability, security, scalability, performance, resilience, supportability, lifecycle, cost, schedule, licensing, vendor, and operational criteria.
  • Document alternatives, evaluation criteria, assumptions, findings, risks, dependencies, and recommendations.
  • Identify capability gaps, technology-integration opportunities, modernization options, and reuse opportunities.
  • Develop architecture decision records and obtain appropriate stakeholder review and approval.
  • Define system, application, service, data, security, deployment, and integration architecture.
  • Develop or oversee system context, logical, physical, deployment, data-flow, trust-boundary, sequence, component, and interface diagrams.
  • Develop and maintain System Design Documents and architecture-design sections.
  • Define architecture patterns, standards, reference models, design principles, and reusable technical approaches.
  • Review technical designs for alignment with enterprise architecture, validated requirements, security standards, and operational constraints.
  • Define and document external and internal interface requirements.
  • Develop or oversee Interface Control Documents and Interface Design Documents.
  • Identify interface participants, protocols, data structures, message patterns, authentication methods, dependencies, service levels, error handling, versioning, and ownership.
  • Evaluate API, event, batch, file-transfer, database, identity, network, and third-party integration approaches.
  • Coordinate interface requirements with application owners, mission partners, external agencies, vendors, and technical teams.
  • Ensure interfaces are designed for security, maintainability, observability, backward compatibility, and controlled evolution.
  • Develop scalability and extensibility approaches.
  • Assess anticipated demand, mission criticality, transaction volume, data growth, concurrency, integration load, and performance requirements.
  • Define approaches for horizontal and vertical scaling, elasticity, capacity management, modularity, reuse, and controlled expansion.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce or retire unused or excess capacity.
  • Ensure architecture supports sustainability, high availability, COOP, backup, recovery, and established service-level requirements.
  • Evaluate single points of failure, capacity constraints, resilience gaps, recovery dependencies, and operational risks.
  • Define architectural requirements for monitoring, logging, alerting, supportability, fault isolation, and service restoration.
  • Develop technical inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.
  • Define architecture scope, assumptions, technical components, environments, interfaces, dependencies, licenses, infrastructure, cloud services, labor considerations, migration activities, testing, security, training, and sustainment needs.
  • Coordinate with program and financial personnel to translate technical architecture into defensible ROM assumptions.
  • Identify uncertainty, cost drivers, risk allowances, implementation phases, and alternative approaches.
  • Develop or review Bills of Materials for required software tools, licenses, cloud services, infrastructure, and development resources.
  • Develop modernization roadmaps and transition architectures.
  • Define implementation phases, architecture increments, technical dependencies, sequencing, interim states, migration considerations, and retirement activities.
  • Support planning for transitions from legacy and on-premises capabilities to approved centralized, cloud, hybrid, or modernized environments.
  • Assess migration readiness and identify architecture changes required before transition.
  • Support the design, establishment, use, and decommissioning of development, integration, testing, staging, and operational environments.
  • Ensure preproduction environments adequately represent interfaces, dependencies, configurations, security controls, performance conditions, and operational constraints.
  • Support architecture and design activities within Agile software-development processes.
  • Provide architectural guidance during release and Sprint planning, backlog refinement, design, development, integration, testing, and demonstrations.
  • Help teams translate architecture requirements into technical user stories, enablers, acceptance criteria, and implementation tasks.
  • Maintain an architecture runway supporting current delivery and anticipated mission needs.
  • Review Sprint outputs for architecture alignment and identify required corrective or follow-on work.
  • Participate in architecture reviews, system-design reviews, interface reviews, security reviews, technical interchange meetings, release-readiness reviews, and demonstrations.
  • Coordinate with cybersecurity personnel to incorporate security architecture, trust boundaries, access controls, data protection, logging, vulnerability management, and applicable RMF controls.
  • Ensure architectural solutions account for applicable Federal and DoD software standards and DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides.
  • Evaluate security impacts throughout the system lifecycle and document architecture-level risks and mitigations.
  • Ensure architecture documentation remains aligned with configuration baselines, approved changes, deployed systems, and operational realities.
  • Maintain architecture repositories, diagrams, standards, decision records, models, plans, and supporting documentation.
  • Communicate complex architectural concepts through clear technical documents, visual models, briefings, workshops, and recommendations.
  • Present architecture options, risks, dependencies, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Provide architecture accomplishments, decisions, risks, issues, dependencies, and modernization status for program reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, systems engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • Minimum of ten years of relevant experience in enterprise architecture, systems architecture, systems engineering, solution architecture, software architecture, or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience developing enterprise or system Concepts of Operations.
  • Experience conducting technical analyses and trade studies.
  • Experience decomposing mission or business needs into functional, component, interface, security, performance, and derived requirements.
  • Experience defining and documenting system and external-interface requirements.
  • Experience supporting complex systems integration across software, data, infrastructure, cloud, network, security, or external systems.
  • Experience designing scalable, extensible, resilient, and supportable enterprise solutions.
  • Experience developing technical assumptions and inputs for rough-order-of-magnitude estimates.
  • Experience developing current-state, target-state, and transition architectures.
  • Experience producing or reviewing architecture diagrams, System Design Documents, Interface Control Documents, Interface Design Documents, requirements-traceability records, and architecture decision records.
  • Experience communicating architecture decisions, options, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, technical-writing, presentation, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • CISSP-ISSAP certification.
  • CISSP-ISSEP certification.
  • A certification formerly recognized for DoD 8570.01-M IASAE Level III and aligned to the applicable current DoD 8140 work role and proficiency level.
  • TOGAF certification.
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional.
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert.
  • Google Professional Cloud Architect.
  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional certification.
  • International Council on Systems Engineering certification, such as Certified Systems Engineering Professional.
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense enterprise architecture or systems-engineering programs.
  • Experience applying DoD Architecture Framework, Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework, or comparable architecture methods.
  • Experience with architecture-modeling languages or tools such as ArchiMate, SysML, UML, Cameo, Sparx Enterprise Architect, or comparable platforms.
  • Experience with Zero Trust, identity architecture, cloud architecture, DevSecOps, data architecture, API management, or enterprise integration.
  • Experience supporting RMF authorization, DISA STIG compliance, COOP, disaster recovery, or mission-resilience planning.
  • Experience working with multiple Agile software-development teams.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation or higher certification.

Skills and Competencies

  • Enterprise and systems architecture.
  • CONOPS and operational-concept development.
  • Structured requirements analysis and decomposition.
  • Technical trade studies and alternative analysis.
  • Interface and integration architecture.
  • Scalability, extensibility, resilience, and capacity planning.
  • Technical estimation and ROM development.
  • Current-state, target-state, and transition-roadmap development.
  • Architecture governance and design reviews.
  • Security architecture and risk analysis.
  • Technical modeling, documentation, and visualization.
  • Government stakeholder facilitation and executive communication.
  • Strong judgment in balancing mission, security, interoperability, cost, schedule, and technical sustainability.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.

However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.

Responsibilities

Product strategy & roadmap ownership

  • Define clear product requirements, intended outcomes and success criteria for development initiatives.
  • Balance stakeholder requests while providing clear rationale for what is pursued, why it matters and how success will be measured.

Metrics, insights & performance

  • Define and track product KPIs and objectives aligned with customer and business outcomes.
  • Use customer feedback, market intelligence, competitive insights and product performance data to identify improvement opportunities and prioritize investments.
  • Provide product performance updates, trend analysis and recommendations to stakeholders and leadership.

Customer engagement & advocacy

  • Partner with customers, Applications, Commercial and technical teams to understand user workflows, unmet needs and market opportunities.
  • Translate customer insights into product requirements, business recommendations and roadmap priorities.
  • Drive solutions that improve customer outcomes and support connected bioprocessing workflows across process development and manufacturing.

Product development, quality & lifecycle management

  • Partner with Commercial, Applications, Operations and other cross-functional teams to support successful product launches and commercialization activities.

Stakeholder communication & enablement

  • Proactively surface cross-functional dependencies and recommend actions or tradeoffs.
  • Support internal product training, customer presentations and enablement activities for Commercial, Applications, Service and Support teams.

  • Experience with spectroscopy, analytical instruments, connected products or hardware-and-software solutions preferred.
  • Ability to translate customer and technical needs into practical product requirements and business recommendations.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams in a matrixed organization.

  • Customer-facing experience and the ability to build effective internal and external relationships.

Skills & Competencies:

  • Experience owning customer escalations with empathy, clarity, urgency, and disciplined follow-through.
  • Demonstrated ownership of strategic support initiatives that improve efficiency, customer satisfaction, quality, and scalability.
  • Ability to translate company objectives into measurable team goals, operating plans, and individual expectations.
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience building or using dashboards, interpreting performance data, identifying root causes, and adjusting team priorities based on evidence.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, with the ability to tailor messaging for employees, customers, executives, and cross-functional stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Experience monitoring team KPIs, service-level performance, ticket queues, or team capacity and using available data to support improvement plans.
